calls.head: Like for like: Martinook vs. Meyers
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Martinook’s line (Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Martinook) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Kraken’s fourth line is Nyman, Meyers and Winterton.

calls.head: The Hurricanes should drive the play
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Kraken one of the worst. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Kraken’s end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina an 83% chance, and they delivered.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle only a 17% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Hurricanes cruise past the Kraken
paras: Jackson Blake got the scoring started for the Hurricanes on the power play midway through the first. Mark Jankowski extended the lead to 2-0 late in the period, and Andrei Svechnikov made it 3-0 on the power play early in the second. Matty Beniers got the Kraken on the board just over four minutes later. Svechnikov scored again on the power play just under four minutes later to make it 4-1 for the Canes. Seattle pulled Joey Daccord after four goals and turned to Philipp Grubauer for the rest of the second. Jankowski struck again midway through the third to make it 5-1 for the Hurricanes. Nikolaj Ehlers finished with three assists.

No fluke here. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Hurricanes win about four in five. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 12 saves for the Hurricanes. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Shayne Gostisbehere, by our Swing measure.

The Hurricanes went 3-for-5 on the power play. The Kraken killed off a two-man advantage that lasted a minute and a half early in the first. The Hurricanes improved to 16-3-2, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Kraken fell to 9-8-1, slipping to fifth in the Pacific.
